page.title: Workflow map
page.intro: How workflows chain together: what the platform detects on its own in the n8n JSON (called sub-workflow, sub-workflow plugged into an AI agent, HTTP call to another workflow's webhook) and the links you add by hand for sequences the JSON doesn't show.
page.hideIsolatedHint: Hides workflows that have no link shown.
page.entryPointsHint: Adds in front of each workflow what starts it: the public URL if it's callable (webhook, form, chat), otherwise “scheduled”, the third-party app, or a manual start. A workflow called by a parent has none — that's already an arrow. These pills don't count as links: they don't stop a workflow from being “isolated”.
page.monitoredHint: Shows only envs declared “monitored” (prod, by default): the other copies of the same business workflow have the same call graph and doubled the map. A workflow whose environment is unknown stays visible.
page.hideArchivedHint: Workflows archived in n8n (hidden from its list) no longer run: their outgoing calls are removed from the diagram. They stay visible if a live workflow calls them — that's then a dead call to fix.

help.intro: This page shows only workflows and how they chain together — not bases or APIs (that's the job of the Dependencies page). It answers: “who triggers whom, and in what order does it run?”

detected.title: Automatically detected links
detected.execute: calls Execute Workflow node: the workflow triggers another one as a sub-workflow.
detected.tool: AI tool sub-workflow plugged in as a tool on an AI agent (Call n8n Workflow Tool node).
detected.webhook: webhook HTTP Request node that hits another workflow's webhook URL (matched on the webhook path).
detected.context: When the call doesn't come from a regular flow, the arrow says where it comes from rather than what it is, followed by the number of nodes in that part of the workflow: loop (3) the calling node is inside a loop, the call fires once per iteration; manual (2) its only trigger is the Execute workflow button — it's a test button, not a production sequence (typically the node that hits its own workflow's webhook, hence the false recursions); sub-workflow (5) the branch is only triggered by another workflow, the call only fires if the parent runs.
detected.recomputed: Detection is recomputed every time the page opens from the synced workflows: there's no “rebuild” button here. A workflow changed in n8n shows up as soon as it has been resynced from the Workflows page.

manual.title: Manual links
manual.body: manual link what the JSON will never tell: a workflow that triggers another through a third-party tool (Make, Zapier, an external cron, a human action), two workflows that must run in a precise order, or a business dependency you want written down somewhere. “Add a link” button → source workflow, target workflow, label shown on the arrow, note. These links are stored in the database: they survive resyncs and follow the workflow if it's renamed.

reading.title: Reading the diagram
reading.lines: Solid line = detected link. Dotted = link you added yourself.
reading.frames: Blue frame = active workflow; grey = workflow disabled in n8n; dotted grey = archived.
reading.triggers: Under the name, how it starts: scheduled, webhook, form, chat, app (Telegram, Gmail…), error, sub-workflow — several if the workflow has several triggers, disabled triggers excluded. no active trigger means nothing can start it anymore. manual test is shown last and doesn't count toward the workflow's nature: an “Execute workflow” button is for testing, not for running — a sub-workflow · manual test workflow is still a sub-workflow (purple frame).
reading.subWorkflow: Purple frame = sub-workflow: it never runs on its own, its only trigger is When Executed by Another Workflow. If it has no incoming arrow, nothing calls it anymore.
reading.self: A workflow that calls itself as a sub-workflow has no arrow looping back to its box: the target is drawn separately, in dotted purple “itself, as a sub-workflow”. It's the same workflow, restarted by the first one — often a branch that processes a list and calls the workflow back row by row (the arrow label then reads loop (n)).
reading.archived: Hide archived (on by default) — a workflow archived in n8n is hidden from the n8n list and no longer runs, but its JSON still contains its calls: without this filter, it clutters the diagram with dead links. It stays visible if it's called by a live workflow, because that's then a real problem to fix. Watch out for namesakes: when an archived and a live workflow share a name, the displayed name is completed with the instance or the n8n id.
reading.entryPoints: Dotted green pill upstream = what starts the workflow that doesn't come from the map: the public URL when it's callable (webhook, form, chat), otherwise scheduled, the third-party app (Telegram, Gmail…), a workflow's error or started by hand. One pill per trigger: a workflow that is both webhook and form has two, there's nothing to pick between. A workflow called by a parent has none — that's already an arrow. These pills don't count as links: a workflow that only has those stays “isolated”. Entry points toggle to hide them.
reading.outOfScope: Dotted orange frame = out-of-scope target: a called workflow that isn't (or no longer) synced, or that lives on another instance. It's often the sign of a broken call — worth checking.
reading.isolated: Hide isolated (on by default) hides workflows with no link at all. Uncheck it to get the full inventory.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.expression: A workflowId built by an expression can't be resolved: that link has to be added by hand.
limits.webhook: Webhook calls are matched by path, but only if the URL targets an instance the platform knows. A call to another n8n installation is shown with its full URL, as an out-of-scope target. Two known instances exposing the same path can still be confused.
limits.scope: The instance selector at the top of the app restricts the map to a single instance; links leaving it then show as out of scope.
